thread:
Lauren Bishop: quick pricing/packaging alignment for Dedicated Burst before we freeze GA messaging. pulling in @Chris Osei @Laura Bennett @Rishi Malhotra @Michael Grant @Sofia Mendes @Stephanie Nguyen @Lukas Meyer @Rachel Kim @Miguel Santos @Markus Klein

Lauren Bishop: goal: confirm (1) what Sales can promise for GA, (2) how we describe limits/denials, (3) contract language needs. pls reply inline if anything is off.

Chris Osei: summarizing what we have in the packaging draft (as of yesterday):
- Burst is an add-on for Dedicated tenants, enabled per-tenant.
- Customer has a baseline reserved capacity; burst lets them temporarily exceed baseline by borrowing from Redwood-managed burst pools in-region.
- Guardrails apply: per-tenant burst cap, max burst ratio vs baseline, cooldown window, and fleet safety caps.
- Metering: burst usage measured separately from baseline, billed as a line item.

Laura Bennett: from Finance side: ok with GA as long as (a) we keep it clearly “paid” + separately metered, and (b) Sales does not imply guaranteed burst availability at any moment.

Rishi Malhotra: +1. pricing assumption we reviewed: burst unit rate > baseline reserved rate to reflect peak procurement + opportunity cost. final band we approved is in the finance thread, but for this thread: we’re good to message “premium rate vs baseline” and avoid hard numbers in public docs.

Stephanie Nguyen: for Sales enablement, we need a crisp “what can I promise?” statement. deals are asking for language like “2x capacity on demand” which is risky.

Lauren Bishop: agreed. proposal for GA promise (pls confirm):
- We can promise: “ability to request burst up to your contracted burst limit when burst pools have capacity, with clear denial reasons when unavailable.”
- We cannot promise: “always available,” “reserved burst,” or “instant scale.”
- We can also promise: “burst is constrained to the same region + hardware class as your Dedicated deployment (no cross-region).”

Lukas Meyer: can we say “best effort” and still be competitive? EMEA prospects want black-and-white.

Rachel Kim: CS POV: we have to be explicit that denials are expected behavior and not an outage, otherwise we’ll get escalations every Monday peak.

Miguel Santos: +1, and we need a customer-facing doc snippet for “what happens when you hit burst cap” (429 vs queue/backpressure) so they handle retries correctly.

Markus Klein: solutions perspective: customers will ask “how do I make sure batch jobs complete?” we should steer them to either (a) raise baseline or (b) schedule jobs with backoff, since we’re not doing reservations for burst in v1.

Chris Osei: on packaging naming: are we settled on “Burst Limit” and “Burst Ratio” as the canonical terms? would help keep Sales + Console + contract consistent.

Michael Grant: legal perspective: we need definitions to avoid ambiguity:
- “Dedicated Baseline Capacity” (reserved)
- “Burst Capacity” (temporary, borrowed)
- “Burst Limit” (per-tenant cap)
- “Admission Control” + “Denial”
Also important: clarify this is not a commitment of additional dedicated GPUs; it’s access to shared burst pools subject to safeguards.

Sofia Mendes: and we should explicitly carve out that “Burst Capacity” is not part of the uptime/latency SLA for the baseline Dedicated service (unless we add a separate SLO/credit scheme, which I don’t think we are for GA).

Lauren Bishop: correct — no SLA credits tied to burst availability for GA. baseline Dedicated SLA remains unchanged. burst is an add-on with documented behavior + denial reasons.

Laura Bennett: that matches approvals. just make sure contract and enablement both say it the same way.

Stephanie Nguyen: ok but we still need something Sales can say besides “it might deny.” can we message “designed for predictable peaks” + “most customers see X% successful admissions”? (even if X is internal)

Lauren Bishop: I’m ok saying “designed for predictable peaks” and “admission controlled” but not giving success % until we have GA data + regional breakdown. we can offer guidance: if you need guaranteed peak headroom, you should reserve it.

Rishi Malhotra: +1. avoid % promises. also avoid wording like “burst guarantees your weekly launch.”

Chris Osei: decision check (packaging):
1) Burst is opt-in add-on for Dedicated
2) Metered separately as “Burst Usage” line item
3) Contract describes it as best-effort access to shared burst pools, subject to admission control
4) No SLA credits for burst availability in GA
can everyone 👍 if aligned

Laura Bennett: 👍

Rishi Malhotra: 👍

Michael Grant: 👍

Sofia Mendes: 👍

Rachel Kim: 👍

Miguel Santos: 👍

Stephanie Nguyen: 👍 (with the ask that we give Sales a tight script)

Lukas Meyer: 👍

Markus Klein: 👍

Lauren Bishop: re: “what happens when denied” — current product behavior is: if request would exceed baseline and burst is denied, we return overload/limit response (429) with a structured denial reason code. we are NOT queueing requests server-side for GA.

Miguel Santos: can we add a one-liner for customer comms: “treat burst denial like rate limiting; retry with exponential backoff + jitter, and fall back to baseline throughput.”

Lauren Bishop: yes. @Miguel Santos can you + @Rachel Kim incorporate that into CS onboarding checklist + canned response?

Rachel Kim: yep, will add to the onboarding checklist and macros.

Stephanie Nguyen: on script: I’ll update enablement one-pager with:
- when to recommend burst (predictable peaks, batch windows)
- when not to (strict guarantees)
- exact wording on best-effort + denial expected + no cross-region

Lukas Meyer: pls include an EMEA-friendly version (customers ask about “hard limits” a lot). I’ll review.

Michael Grant: contract items we need from Product by EOW:
- exact defined terms (Baseline, Burst Capacity, Burst Limit)
- statement that burst is subject to platform safeguards and may be denied
- statement that baseline SLA unaffected; burst availability not SLA-backed
- billing: separate line item, and what the metering unit is (don’t need the rate in the contract, but define the unit)

Sofia Mendes: also: we should include an “abuse / neighbor protection” clause: customer agrees not to circumvent guardrails (e.g., request splitting) and acknowledges we may throttle/deny to protect service.

Chris Osei: on metering unit: current plan is usage-based on burst allocation time (internally gpu-seconds) converted to billing units. we’ll describe it as “Burst Usage” measured per second/minute of burst capacity allocated to your tenant. (wording tbd, but concept is that it’s not tokens.)

Laura Bennett: prefer we keep unit definition stable and auditable. if we say “per minute of burst capacity consumed” that’s easier to reason about than tokens.

Lauren Bishop: ok — we’ll align doc + Console labels around “Burst Usage (capacity time)” and avoid token language.

Stephanie Nguyen: last question: can Sales promise a max ratio (like “up to 2x”)?

Lauren Bishop: we can promise “up to your contracted burst limit.” we should not blanket promise “2x” across the board; configs vary by region/hardware and customer tier. if a deal needs 2x, it must be written into their Order Form as the Burst Limit.

Lukas Meyer: got it — so default script: “Burst is configurable; we’ll contract a Burst Limit (cap) appropriate for your baseline and region.”

Michael Grant: perfect. we’ll make sure the Order Form references Burst Limit and avoids vague multipliers.

Lauren Bishop: action items:
- @Michael Grant/@Sofia Mendes draft contract language stub w/ definitions + burst carve-out (EOW)
- @Stephanie Nguyen/@Lukas Meyer update enablement one-pager with approved GA promise + denial messaging (early next week)
- @Chris Osei update packaging doc: terminology + billing unit + “no queueing; 429 + reason codes” (today)
- @Rachel Kim/@Miguel Santos update CS onboarding checklist + macros re: retries/backoff + how to interpret denial reason codes (this week)

Lauren Bishop: thanks all. once these are updated I’ll reply in the GA readiness thread with “pricing/packaging locked” and link the docs.

Chris Osei: will do. I’ll also add a short FAQ entry: “Is burst guaranteed?” → “No; best-effort; reserve baseline for guarantees.”

Stephanie Nguyen: 👍 I’ll ping Sales leadership with the final script once the doc is updated.

Michael Grant: please also send me the exact customer-facing phrasing you want; we’ll mirror it in the contract where appropriate.

Lauren Bishop: will send the final snippet after @Chris Osei updates packaging doc.
